key_insight: Reward learning for autonomous agents is more robust when teaching spans multiple environments and uses comparison feedback, which constrains reward functions more globally than demonstrations alone.
engineering_relevance: This suggests practical reward-model training should combine environment selection with low-cost human feedback to improve deployment robustness across changing operating conditions.
method: Greedily choose informative environments that reveal complementary reward constraints.
Query the most cost-effective feedback modality within each selected environment.
Use a hierarchical teaching strategy to learn rewards that generalize across MDPs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method achieves substantially lower regret and better held-out-environment generalization than uniform teaching baselines under the same feedback budget.
watch_item: Environment selection and feedback querying may be sensitive to MDP coverage and cost assumptions, so gains may depend on how well the training environments represent deployment shifts.
paper_title: Multi-Modal, Multi-Environment Machine Teaching for Robust Reward Learning
